lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say introduces the target vocabulary through audio modeling and repetition. Then practise provides initial controlled practice of the new question and answer structure using the new words.
Look for clear pronunciation of the new food words and accurate use of ‘Have you got any…?’ during the practice phase.
“I’m having a BBQ! What do I need?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to questions about possession. It builds accuracy with ‘Has he/she got any...?"’ and short answers.
Look for accurate use of ‘Has he/she got any…?’, correct short answers (‘Yes, he has / No, she hasn’t’), and clear pronunciation of the food items.
“I want to make burgers! I’ll ask my friends to bring the other ingredients.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Unscramble and write

details: Unscramble and write consolidates vocabulary recognition and spelling accuracy.
Look for correct identification of the images and accurate spelling of the target words on the lines.
“Can you help me write out a list of everything I need to ask them to bring, so I don’t forget?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - B Look and connect

details: Look and connect checks understanding of sentence structure and word order. Students carefully link words to form correct questions and short answers based on the visual cues.
Look for accurate connections between the words to form grammatically correct sentences and appropriate short answers matching the pictures.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - Speaking Sandwich Bingo

details: Sandwich Bingo motivates students to use the target language through gamification. Students create a personalised board and practise asking ‘Have you got any...?’ to achieve the winning pattern.
Look for active interaction between pairs, accurate question formation, clear pronunciation, and correct identification of the winning 'X' pattern.
“Time to BBQ! Let’s make our burgers. Yummy!”
